name: Learning the Rule the Hard Way
summary: The ordinary world stops working according to its old rules — the dead walk, the sky changes, the network dies, the tide does not go out — and the first lesson is paid for with somebody. From that death a rule is inferred and stated aloud, and the group survives to the next chapter precisely to the extent that they obey a rule they cannot yet explain.

roles.label: the one who infers the rule
constraints: has only one data point to work from

roles.label: the one whose death taught it
the changed world
constraints: gives no warnings and no second chances

beats.label: The ordinary stops working
beats.intent: the familiar world visibly ceases to behave as it should

beats.label: The first lesson costs someone
beats.intent: a death demonstrates a boundary nobody knew existed

beats.label: The rule is inferred
beats.intent: a provisional rule is stated aloud from a single instance

beats.label: Survive by obeying it
beats.intent: the group lives by a rule it cannot yet explain

preconditions.text: a world whose operating rules have changed without notice

effects.text: the group holds a working rule that is not yet understood
the cost of learning each further rule is now known to be a life

examples.text: Nobody knew why the ones who ran were taken and the ones who stood still were not, but by the second day nobody ran.

name: Not Enough for Everyone
summary: A resource that keeps people alive — water, insulin, seats, ammunition, fuel — is counted and found short, and the shortfall has names attached to it. The allocation is made by people who have to keep living with each other afterwards, and what the group learns about itself in that hour outlasts the resource by a long way.

roles.label: the one who must decide
constraints: will have to live with those excluded

roles.label: those who do not get it

beats.label: The count comes up short
beats.intent: the shortfall is established as an arithmetic fact

beats.label: The shortfall has names
beats.intent: the abstraction resolves into specific people

beats.label: The allocation is made
beats.intent: someone decides, by whatever principle they can defend

beats.label: The excluded remember
beats.intent: the decision becomes a permanent fact of the group

preconditions.text: a countable resource and more claimants than units

effects.text: the group's real hierarchy is now visible to everyone in it
the excluded have a grievance with a name attached

examples.text: There were nine doses and eleven people, and the argument took four minutes, and nobody ever spoke about it again.

name: The Shelter That Charges
summary: A refuge is found that is genuinely safe — walls, food, warmth, a lock that works — and the relief is real. Then the terms emerge: a labour, an obedience, a person handed over, a rule about who is allowed to leave. The group must weigh a certain safety against a price they cannot pay indefinitely.

beats.label: Refuge is found
beats.intent: a genuinely safe place is reached and the relief is real

beats.label: Trust is extended
beats.intent: the group commits to staying and gives something up to do so

beats.label: The terms emerge
beats.intent: the price of remaining becomes clear

beats.label: Pay it or leave
beats.intent: certain safety is weighed against an unpayable price

preconditions.text: a group with no viable alternative to the shelter offered

effects.text: the group has either submitted to terms or is exposed again
what each member was willing to accept is now known to the others

examples.text: The gate closed behind them and the food was hot and real, and in the morning someone explained about the work rota, and about the rule.

name: One of Us Is Already Gone
summary: Someone in the group is infected, turned, informing, or otherwise no longer safe, and the test that would prove it is unreliable, slow, or does not exist. Suspicion does the work that evidence cannot, the group turns on the most plausible rather than the actual, and the wrong call costs more than the compromise would have.

roles.label: the group that must decide
constraints: cannot verify what it needs to know

roles.label: the most plausible suspect
constraints: is plausible for reasons unrelated to the truth

beats.label: A sign appears
beats.intent: evidence emerges that one of the group is no longer safe

beats.label: The test fails them
beats.intent: no reliable way exists to identify who

beats.label: Suspicion picks a target
beats.intent: the group converges on the most plausible rather than the actual

beats.label: The wrong call lands
beats.intent: the decision is executed and its error becomes visible

preconditions.text: a threat that hides inside the group and resists verification

effects.text: the group has acted irreversibly on a guess
the actual compromise is still present and now harder to raise

examples.text: They watched each other's hands for three days, and in the end it was the man nobody had watched who did not wake up right.

name: Someone Is Asking to Come In
summary: An outsider asks for entry with a story that may or may not be true, and both answers are defensible: opening the door risks everyone, closing it kills someone who is asking. The choice is made under time pressure with incomplete information, and the consequence — whichever way — is charged to the person who made it.

roles.label: the one who answers the door
the one asking
constraints: their story cannot be checked in time

beats.label: Someone asks to come in
beats.intent: an outsider requests entry with an uncheckable story

beats.label: Compassion against arithmetic
beats.intent: both answers are shown to be defensible

beats.label: The door opens or does not
beats.intent: the decision is made under time pressure

beats.label: It is charged to the decider
beats.intent: the outcome attaches to the person who chose

preconditions.text: a defended place and an outsider whose account cannot be verified in time

effects.text: the group's threshold for admitting strangers is now set by precedent
the decider carries a specific outcome personally

examples.text: She was still talking through the door when they voted, and afterwards nobody could agree on how long the voice had gone on.

name: Authority Made in an Afternoon
summary: Nobody is in charge and a decision cannot wait, so someone makes it — not the strongest or the most senior, but whoever was willing to say a sentence out loud while everyone else was still looking at each other. The decision turns out well enough, and authority is granted retroactively by people who will resent it later.

roles.label: the decision that could not wait
constraints: had to be made before it could be discussed

beats.label: Nobody is in charge
beats.intent: a decision is required and no authority exists to make it

beats.label: Someone says it out loud
beats.intent: a person with no standing states what will be done

beats.label: The decision holds
beats.intent: the choice works well enough that nobody reverses it

beats.label: Authority granted, resentment banked
beats.intent: leadership is conceded by people who will resent conceding it

preconditions.text: a group with no established authority facing a decision that cannot wait

effects.text: a leader now exists whose legitimacy rests on one afternoon
those who deferred have a grievance available to them later

examples.text: He said 'we go north' and started walking, and eleven people followed him, and that was the entire process.

name: A Thing From Before
summary: An object from the world that ended surfaces — a photograph, a working radio, a jar of something sweet, a child's shoe — and it is worthless by every survival calculus and priceless by every other. What people are willing to spend to keep it says more about where they are than any inventory does.

roles.label: the one who wants to keep it
constraints: cannot justify it on survival terms

roles.label: the one who counts the cost

beats.label: The relic surfaces
beats.intent: an object from the ended world is found

beats.label: Worthless and priceless
beats.intent: its uselessness and its meaning are both stated plainly

beats.label: What keeping it costs
beats.intent: a real price is named for carrying it further

beats.label: The choice says where they are
beats.intent: the decision reveals how much of the old world they still hold

preconditions.text: a survival calculus strict enough that sentiment has a measurable cost

effects.text: how far the group has travelled from who they were is now explicit
a division exists between those who would spend for meaning and those who would not

examples.text: The radio would never work again and weighed as much as two days of water, and he carried it for nine days before he put it down.
